messages.author: eafa26121223327e
messages.subject: Projection warnings in Mesh
parts:
Hi All,
I understand that R has changed the way they handle Proj4. now. Unfortunately, I haven't been able to figure out how/if this is affecting the SPDE models I'm running. I do think that something under the hood isn't working though because correlations I was running prior to the switch now have substantially different values than before. I've pasted in some code and the associated warnings I've been receiving below. If someone has experienced this before I would appreciate your advice. The bolded red line at the end is the warning that pops up every time the mesh is called into play. 
KK

MF<-readRDS(file=".../MF_4.rda")
MyStd <- function(x) { (x - mean(x,na.rm=TRUE)) / sd(x,na.rm=TRUE)}

# Set seed
set.seed(234234)
train<-fread("...trainingdata.csv")

crs.m<-CRS("+proj=aea +lat_1=40.38611111111111 +lat_2=47.27722222222222 +lat_0=37 +lon_0=-105.6855555555556 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD27 +units=m +no_defs")

crs.km<-CRS("+proj=aea +lat_1=40.38611111111111 +lat_2=47.27722222222222 +lat_0=37 +lon_0=-105.6855555555556 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD27 +units=km +no_defs")

Loc2 <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(train[,5:6],
                    train[,5:6],    
                    proj4string = crs.m)   

Loc<-spTransform(Loc2,crs.km)

ConvHull   <- inla.nonconvex.hull(Loc, convex = 45)
range<-80
max.edge<-c(0.1,0.67)*range
max.edge
mesh<-inla.mesh.2d(loc=Loc,
loc.domain=Loc,
boundary=ConvHull,
max.edge=max.edge,#c(87000,400000),
min.angle=21,
offset = 6,
cutoff=5,crs=crs.km)

50: In showSRID(SRS_string, format = "PROJ", multiline = "NO",  ... :
  Discarded datum unknown in CRS definition

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Projection warnings in Mesh
parts:
Hi,
That code looks like it should still be ok.
Most of the warnings about proj4 are just about the sometimes inability to convert from proj6 to proj4 for display purposes of the CRS. The WKT proj6 information is what’s actually used in transformations etc.
check the cat(wkt()) output for your to CRS objects to see if the proj6 information seems to have incorporated the metres/kilometres information correctly.
The datum specification_may_ be a problem, if the warning comes from the initial conversion from proj4 to proj6; make sure to run your code line by line to isolate what step actually generates the warning.

Finn

Could either of these be causing the issue? 

Thanks,
KK

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Projection warnings in Mesh
parts:
For the most part, the showSRID warnings can be ignored, and the new rgdal version has several functions to turn off these warnings, or limit the amount of them that are shown.
One option is
options("rgdal_show_exportToProj4_warnings"="none")
library(rgdal)
or using
rgdal::set_rgdal_show_exportToProj4_warnings(FALSE)
See ?rgdal::set_rgdal_show_exportToProj4_warnings for more details.

check the cat(wkt()) output for your to CRS objects to see if the proj6 information seems to have incorporated the metres/kilometres information correctly.
The datum specification_may_ be a problem, if the warning comes from the initial conversion from proj4 to proj6; make sure to run your code line by line to isolate what step actually generates the warning.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Projection warnings in Mesh
parts:
Yes, if the warnings appear first with inla.mesh.2d, they are likely ignorable.
Unfortunately, the only safe way of checking these things is to verify that the actually coordinates and mappings themselves are sensible/correct.
E.g. by verifying that a known function is evaluated correctly on the mesh, that the A-matrix has non-zero elements for every data point that's supposed to lie within the mesh.
The way the proj4/proj6 transition works in R is a bit of a mess unfortunately. Do make sure to install the latest sp and rgal, and INLA package versions, since I fed several bug fixes into rgdal and sp triggered by usage commonly seen with INLA.

Finn
